feeds.title: JOHN BANKS' CIVIL WAR BLOG
feeds.description: A civil war blog focused on Connecticut, Antietam, Gettysburg and stories of common soldiers.

feeds.title: The Civil War Picket
feeds.description: Fascinated by the Civil War since childhood, I used to terrorize my children by dragging them to battlefields across the South. I am a writer, editor and web producer. Follow this blog for civil war news, preservation, events, locations and photos.

feeds.title: Dan Masters' Civil War Chronicles
feeds.description: The study of the Civil War is a never ending but most pleasant journey through the libraries, historical societies, museums, cemeteries, backroads, and forgotten spaces of America. This blog captures the results of those journeys in the form of battle narratives written predominantly by Ohioans.

feeds.title: Irish in the American Civil War Blog
feeds.description: The Irish in the American Civil War blog was set up to explore the experience of the Irish in the American Civil War, and to also act as a resource for those interested in the topic.

feeds.title: My Civil War Obsession
feeds.description: I started this blog to explore the Civil War and why it fascinates me so much. I have a B.A. in History from the University of KentuckyFollow this blog to read and learn about the civil war, local history, and genealogy and try to use this platform to find new and interesting stories to share or to help develop opinions and beliefs.

feeds.title: Civil War Books and Authors
feeds.description: Civil War Books and Authors is a non-fiction American Civil War book review journal, with commentary, publishing news, interviews, reading lists, and profiles of upcoming releases.

feeds.title: A Mostly Civil War Blog
feeds.description: Conner, a longtime journalist, is the author of a 2018 novel 'The Last Circle of Ulysses Grant', published by Square Circle Press. He also wrote a 2013 biography 'General Gordon Granger' published by Casemate. He is currently writing a biography of the Kansas abolitionist and Civil War Colonel James Montgomery. Follow this blog to know more about civil war.

feeds.title: Civil War Memory
feeds.description: Kevin M. Levin is an award-winning educator and historian based in Boston, Massachusetts. He has written extensively about the American Civil War, promotes understanding of the most important period in American history and to challenge people to think more critically about the civil war.

feeds.title: Civil War Quilts
feeds.description: This blog gives detailed information about the Reproduction Quilts & Fabric. Discover the collection of the civil war quilts by following our feed.

feeds.title: The Library of Congress Blog » Civil War
feeds.description: The Library of Congress is the largest library in the world, with millions of books, recordings, photographs, newspapers, maps, and manuscripts in its collections. The Library preserves and provides access to a rich, diverse and enduring source of knowledge to inform, inspire and engage you in your intellectual and creative endeavors. Follow this blog to get more information about the civil war.

feeds.title: Emerging Civil War Blog
feeds.description: Emerging Civil War serves as a public history-oriented platform for sharing original scholarship related to the American Civil War. Follow this blog for original and free content for civil war scholars, historians, and enthusiasts!

feeds.title: Student of the American Civil War
feeds.description: I'm a retired U. S. Air Force officer, former Human Resources Manager with a global company, and currently an educator. I developed an interest in the American Civil War while a college student. Since then I've collected books, videos, CDs, and magazines about the civil war. Follow this blog for reflections on learning about the civil war.

feeds.title: Civil War Buckles & Artifacts
feeds.description: I've been collecting civil war memorabilia for over 50 years. My areas of interest include antebellum and civil war buckles and buttons, and Gettysburg relics. This site provides authentic civil war artifacts and items for sale. Follow this blog for interesting artifacts about civil war.

feeds.title: Bull Runnings
feeds.description: Bull Runnings is the first battle of bull run's digital history project. I also post thoughts on the project and commentary on the campaign and the civil war.

feeds.title: Civil War Bookshelf
feeds.description: American Civil War historiography and publishing blogged by Dimitri Rotov. Get more information about civil war by following this feed.

feeds.title: Teaching the Civil War Blog
feeds.description: I am an educational technologist, a blogger, podcaster and expert in using technology to teach history with a particular interest in the American Civil War. This blog provides lesson plans, resources, videos, tools, tips, and strategies for teaching the American Civil War.

feeds.title: Regular Cavalry in the Civil War
feeds.description: Regular Cavalry in the Civil War focuses on Civil War cavalry, primarily oriented on the Union regular cavalry regiments. Will feature biographical sketches, discussions of engagements, unit histories, letters, journals, and a database of those who served in the regiments during the Civil War as I'm able to compile them. I am a retired Army officer and amateur Civil War historian. I focus my studies on the Regular cavalry regiments because I served in one of them and because they haven't received the in-depth coverage that their volunteer brethren have.

feeds.title: Chickamauga Blog
feeds.description: David A. Powell is a graduate of the Virginia Military Institute, class of 1983, with a BA in history. After graduating he went to work in the family business, CBS Messenger, in the Chicago area, but David never lost his intense interest in military history, especially in the American Civil War. He has published articles in a number of magazines, more than fifteen historical simulations of various battles, and led tours to various sites. For the past decade David's focus has been on the epic battle of Chickamauga.

feeds.title: The Journal of the Civil War Era
feeds.description: The Journal of the Civil War Era is published by UNC Press in association with the George and Ann Richards Civil War Era Center. It publishes the most creative new work on the many issues raised by slavery, the sectional crisis, war, emancipation, Reconstruction, and memory of the country's signal conflict, while bringing fresh understanding to the struggles that defined the period, and by extension, the course of American history in the nineteenth century.

feeds.title: The Reconstruction Era
feeds.description: Blog Exploring the World the Civil War Created. Pat Young is an attorney currently serving as Downstate Advocacy Director at the New York Immigration Coalition and the Special Professor of Immigration Law at Hofstra University School of Law. He is the author of the popular blog series The Immigrants' Civil War.

feeds.title: Cannonball Blog » Civil War
feeds.description: Part of the USA Today Network

feeds.title: Hampton Newsome
feeds.description: This is an infrequent blog about historical research and writing. Check out the history of civil war, regiments, interesting tidbits, old articles and more!

feeds.title: Civil War Memory
feeds.description: Reflections on the history and legacy of America's bloodiest and most divisive conflict. Click to read Civil War Memory, by Kevin M. Levin, a Substack publication with thousands of readers. We are in the midst of a national reckoning surrounding our collective past. Monuments are coming down and states are passing laws in an attempt to control how some of the darkest chapters in our nation's history are taught. Kevin has always been fascinated with this tension between history and memory, especially in connection with the Civil War era.

feeds.title: American Civil War Round Table Blog
feeds.description: Our blog contains a in depth look at the battles, personalities and everything else related to the Civil War. Book Reviews, Event talks, Profiles and so much more. Since our establishment in 1953 the ACW Roundtable (UK) has dedicated itself to the study of the American Civil War. Since 2017 we have been a UK registered charity whose aims are to educate people about all aspects of the war, and to preserve the heritage of the war both in the United Kingdom and in the United States.

feeds.title: National Museum of Civil War Medicine blog
feeds.description: The Nat'l Museum of Civil War Medicine tells the medical story of the Civil War-a story of courage, care, and healing amidst America's bloodiest war. Don't miss out on interesting finds and upcoming events from the National Museum of Civil War Medicine. Read the latest research from experts in the field.

feeds.title: Running the Blockade: A Civil War Naval Blog
feeds.description: All things dealing with the Civil War Navies and actions along the coasts and rivers and against forts. Emphasis will be placed on Fort Fisher and all operations around the Blockade and Running the Blockade.

feeds.title: English Civil War
feeds.description: English Civil War is a hub for resources, comment, and discussion, concentrating primarily on the conflict in England 1642-1649, though occasionally covering other items of interest from the wider early modern period. Get articles, discussion, resources, maps, timelines, events and courses on the English Civil War.

feeds.title: Civil Discourse Blog
feeds.description: Civil Discourse explores the complex history of the long Civil War era by connecting academic and public audiences via engagement with both traditional and new scholarship regarding one of the most transformative eras in American history. Follow this blog to explore the American Civil War.

feeds.title: 85th Pennsylvania in Civil War
feeds.description: Dan Clendaniel,author of Such Hard and Severe Service: The 85th Pennsylvania in the Civil War, is a retired public school teacher from Prince William County, Va. He taught American history and American government in Virginia for 34 years.

feeds.title: Civil War Blog
feeds.description: The Civil War Research Project focuses on the history and genealogy of Upper Dauphin County Pennsylvania veterans and their families in and after the Civil War. Follow to get regular updates from this blog in your inbox.

feeds.title: Civil War Librarian
feeds.description: Rea Andrew Redd is a librarian in the USA. His areas of studies are Civil War Medicine, Abraham Lincoln, U.S. Army Signal Corps, antebellum politics. This blog covers news and classic American Civil War books and media.

feeds.title: Civil War Chat
feeds.description: This blog has detailed information about the chats, articles, and facts that happened during the time of civil war. Get more information about civil war by following our feed.

feeds.title: Civil War Navy
feeds.description: Civil War Navy is a great magazine that will deal with the advancements made in the Naval Warfare during the civil war. We have some of the most knowledgeable civil war experts providing amazing stories and information anxious to help us get started in this adventure.

feeds.title: TOCWOC A Civil War Blog
feeds.description: TOCWOC is a group civil war blog formed in September 2007. Our purpose is to enlighten and entertain readers on every aspect of the civil war, whether it be social, political, military, or another history. Follow to keep up with our blog.

feeds.title: Spotsylvania Civil War Blog
feeds.description: Discussion of all social, political and cultural aspects of the American Civil War battles fought in Spotsylvania County, Virginia. Antebellum to the modern-day perspective of the material culture effects of these engagements, both military and civilian. Follow this blog for monthly updates.

feeds.title: Cryssa Bazos » English Civil War
feeds.description: I am a historical fiction writer and 17th Century enthusiast, with a particular interest in the English Civil War (ECW). I have published a number of articles in the Word Weaver, online E-Zines, Reading as Writers, and the Canadian Authors Association (CAA). Get more information by following this feed.

feeds.title: American Civil War Voices Blog
feeds.description: I am a historical novelist and educator with a focus on daily life during the Civil War period based on original documents and literature of the times. Follow to keep up with the latest from this blog.

feeds.title: Jo Ann Daly Carr
feeds.description: Keep up with articles from Jo Ann Daly Carr.

feeds.title: Civil War Rx
feeds.description: The premier source guide to civil war medicine. Read shocking facts about one million American casualties and the country's massive volunteer relief effort. Follow to get the latest articles from this feed in your inbox.

feeds.title: Dead Confederates
feeds.description: I'm a native-born and lifelong Texan, with some branches of my family here stretching back to the days of the Republic. All of my family, on both sides and going back half-a-dozen generations, are Southerners, from Texas, Virginia, Alabama, Georgia, Florida and elsewhere, with a few border state folks from Missouri thrown in for good measure. This blog is my attempt to explore the conflict and legacy of civil war. This blog exists as much to clarify my own thinking as it is to inform others.

feeds.title: Random Thoughts on History
feeds.description: Tim Talbott's blog features his musings on American, African American, Southern, Civil War, Reconstruction, and Public History topics and books. Including recent aquisitions, recommendations and more. Tim is a life-long history enthusiast with a passion for sharing the educational advantages of learning our past.

feeds.title: Mercer Square
feeds.description: Fredericksburg is perhaps best known for that fateful Civil War battle on December 13, 1862. As a volunteer at the Fredericksburg Battlefield Visitor's Center, I became aware that the visiting public was having trouble visualizing the battlefield due to the present-day built-up nature of the city. My goal is not to provide a comprehensive description of the battle. Rather, to look at various interesting parts more deeply. The initial focus is on the terrain. Later we will explore the roads, buildings, and whatever comes to mind.

feeds.title: American Civil War Museum Blog
feeds.description: The goal of The American Civil War Museum is to help a diverse national and international audience learn American Civil War history in all its breadth and scope. Using dynamic and interactive exhibits, engaging educational programs and historical research, the museum will tell a multitude of military, political and civilian stories of the people of the time.

feeds.title: Civil War Emancipation
feeds.description: In 'Civil War Emancipation' I will commemorate important milestones in emancipation in the Civil War as their 150th anniversary arrives in the sesquicentennial; discuss noteworthy publications on this subject comment on current events related to the Civil War and emancipation plus write on whatever else comes to mind that is appropriate.

feeds.title: Civil War Monitor Blog
feeds.description: The Civil War Monitor is a quarterly magazine devoted to portraying American Civil War history from a variety of perspectives. Readers will find originally researched articles, rare historical images, comprehensive maps, and modern graphics - all geared toward the interests of modern-day Civil War enthusiasts.

feeds.title: Maine at War
feeds.description: Maine and the Civil War
